title: Reto en Ciudad del Cabo: Navidad en verano
goal: a explicar cómo se celebran las fiestas en España y entender las costumbres de Ciudad del Cabo

ex.t: Table Mountain is flat on top, like a table.
ex.es: La Montaña de la Mesa es plana por arriba, como una mesa.

ex.t: We went up the mountain by cable car.
ex.es: Subimos a la montaña en teleférico.

vocab.es: el mantel (la nube que cubre la montaña)

ex.t: The cloud on top of the mountain is called the tablecloth.
ex.es: A la nube que cubre la montaña la llaman «el mantel».

ex.t: On Christmas Day, many families have a braai.
ex.es: El día de Navidad, muchas familias hacen una barbacoa.

ex.t: In South Africa, they have a summer Christmas.
ex.es: En Sudáfrica tienen una Navidad en verano.

ex.t: African penguins can be seen near Cape Town.
ex.es: Cerca de Ciudad del Cabo se pueden ver pingüinos africanos.

vocab.es: el paseo marítimo, la zona del puerto

ex.t: We had dinner at the waterfront.
ex.es: Cenamos en la zona del puerto.

ex.t: The sunset from the mountain was unforgettable.
ex.es: La puesta de sol desde la montaña fue inolvidable.

pron.title: Repaso: acento de frase
pron.tip: Lee con ritmo: palabras importantes fuertes y is / was suaves. The CAble car was OPened in nineteen TWENty-NINE.

exercises.title: Ciudad del Cabo
exercises.text: Cape Town is dominated by Table Mountain, which is flat on top. When a white cloud covers it, locals say the tablecloth is on. The cable car was opened in 1929, and today it is used by thousands of visitors. Christmas is celebrated in summer here, often with a braai on the beach.

questions.q: ¿Qué dicen cuando una nube cubre la montaña?
¿Cómo se celebra a menudo la Navidad allí?
options: Con una barbacoa en la playa
questions.answer: Con una barbacoa en la playa

exercises.q: In Cape Town, Christmas ___ celebrated in summer.
exercises.why: Costumbre que se repite: presente, is celebrated.
Fecha pasada y singular: was opened.

exercises.q: African penguins can ___ seen near Cape Town.
exercises.why: Después de can, el verbo be en su forma base: can be seen.

exercises.q: The cable car is ___ by thousands of visitors every day.
The cloud on top of the mountain is ___ the tablecloth.

exercises.context: Un guía sudafricano te pregunta cuándo se abren los regalos en España.
options: In many homes, they're opened on 6th January.
In many homes, they open on 6th January.
In many homes, they're open on 6th January.
exercises.answer: In many homes, they're opened on 6th January.
exercises.why: Los regalos se abren: are opened (pasiva).

exercises.context: Te preguntan qué se come en España en Nochevieja.
options: Twelve grapes are eaten at midnight.
Twelve grapes were eat at midnight.
exercises.answer: Twelve grapes are eaten at midnight.

exercises.q: The cable car was open in 1929.
exercises.why: Pasiva: was + participio (opened). Open sin -ed significa «abierto».

exercises.q: Yesterday some penguins was seen on the beach.

exercises.es: En Ciudad del Cabo la Navidad se celebra en verano
exercises.answer: In Cape Town Christmas is celebrated in summer

exercises.q: Thousands of tourists visit Table Mountain every year.
answer: Table Mountain is visited by thousands of tourists every year.
Every year Table Mountain is visited by thousands of tourists.
exercises.why: Table Mountain + is visited + by thousands of tourists.

exercises.q: La montaña se puede ver desde toda la ciudad.
answer: The mountain can be seen from the whole city.
The mountain can be seen from all over the city.
The mountain can be seen from everywhere in the city.
exercises.why: Se puede ver = can be seen.

exercises.q: The cable car was opened in 1929.

exercises.t: In Spain, presents are brought by the Three Kings.
exercises.es: En España, los regalos los traen los Reyes Magos.

dialog.title: Navidad con barbacoa
dialog.setting: Yolanda charla con Thandi, una guía, en el teleférico de la Montaña de la Mesa

lines.t: Welcome to Table Mountain! This cable car was opened in 1929.
lines.es: ¡Bienvenida a la Montaña de la Mesa! Este teleférico se inauguró en 1929.

lines.t: Wow! And how is Christmas celebrated here?
lines.es: ¡Vaya! ¿Y cómo se celebra aquí la Navidad?

lines.t: It's summer, so lunch is often cooked on a braai.
lines.es: Es verano, así que la comida se suele hacer en una barbacoa.

lines.t: A barbecue at Christmas! In Spain it's usually cold.
lines.es: ¡Barbacoa en Navidad! En España suele hacer frío.

lines.t: And when are presents opened in Spain?
lines.es: ¿Y cuándo se abren los regalos en España?

lines.t: Many are brought by the Three Kings on 6th January.
lines.es: Muchos los traen los Reyes Magos el 6 de enero.

lines.t: How lovely! Look, the tablecloth is coming.
The cloud! Quick, let's take a photo before it covers everything.
lines.es: ¡La nube! Rápido, hagamos una foto antes de que lo tape todo.

questions.q: ¿Cómo se cocina a menudo la comida de Navidad allí?

realLife.context: Para preguntar por las costumbres locales cuando viajas

summary: Presente pasivo para costumbres: Christmas is celebrated in summer
Pasado pasivo para la historia: The cable car was opened in 1929
Can be seen = se puede ver
Ciudad del Cabo: Table Mountain, the tablecloth, braai, penguins
